question.worked_solution:
We need to remove the radical $\sqrt{y}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{y},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2\sqrt{y}} & = \\ \frac{x}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{y}} & = \\ \frac{x\cdot \sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{y}\cdot \sqrt{y}} & = \\ \frac{x\sqrt{y}}{2(\sqrt{y})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{x\sqrt{y}}{2y}\end{aligned}
$$
